item.title: [7] Strain engineering of transient exciton diffusion in WSe2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures
item.description:
Last authors: Rudolf Bratschitsch, Ermin Malic

Authors: Roberto Rosati, Mohammed Adel Aly, Robert Schmidt, Rudolf Bratschitsch, Ermin Malic

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental control of 2D monolayers, relevant to vdW interests.

Tags: #experiment #WSe2 #monolayer

Abstract: Here, the authors show how strain allows control of the spatiotemporal exciton dynamics in WSe 2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures. They demonstrate that tensile strain abruptly increases the excess energy of hot excitons, thereby accelerating their transient diffusion. The authors trace this back to suppressed phonon-mediated scattering from bright to dark excitons. Furthermore, a periodic modulation of the transient exciton diffusion is predicted in the presence of a compressive strain resulting from emission of M phonons.

item.description:
Last authors: Gianluigi A. Botton, Patrick Fournier

Authors: Maxime Dion, Guo-zhen Zhu, Guillaume Hardy, Gianluigi A. Botton, Patrick Fournier

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental characterization of emerging Mott phases at cuprate interfaces using transport and microscopy.

Tags: #material #cuprates #heterostructure #Mottinsulator

Abstract: The p - n junction is at the heart of the first great technological revolution. Here, the authors fabricate and characterize such a junction made entirely out of cuprates superconductors thin films. They observe a charge transfer between n -type Pr 1 . 85 Ce 0 . 15 CuO 4 and p -type La 1 . 85 Sr 0 . 15 CuO 4 , from which a Mott insulating layer emerges at the atomically sharp interface. They first assess the quality of the structure through x-ray diffraction and scanning transmission electron microscopy and then they explore the nature of the insulating interface arising from strong electron correlations with various electrical transport experiments.

item.title: [9] Correlation-enhanced electron-phonon coupling in FeSe/SrTiO3 at a magic angle
item.description:
Last authors: Lian Li, Subhasish Mandal

Authors: Qiang Zou, Antik Sihi, Basu Dev Oli, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Combines ARPES, STM, and DMFT to study correlation-enhanced superconductivity in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO3.

Tags: #ARPES #STM #FeSe #superconductivity

Abstract: Here, the authors combine first-principles dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), epitaxial materials design, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, and scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy to show that superconductivity in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO 3 is maximized at a magic FeSe 4 tetrahedral angle. They demonstrate that strong electronic correlations, captured by DMFT, substantially enhance electron-phonon coupling within the FeSe layer and produce a superconducting dome. These findings reveal the microscopic origin of enhanced superconductivity and suggest a route for engineering higher-temperature superconductors.

item.description:
Last authors: Koichi Kindo, Takao Watanabe

Authors: Shunpei Yamaguchi, Nae Sasaki, Shintaro Adachi, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental magnetotransport study on high-Tc cuprates investigating the pseudogap origin.

Tags: #material #cuprate #superconductivity #transport

Abstract: Elucidating the origin of the pseudogap remains a central challenge in copper oxide high‑ T c superconductors. By investigating the magnetotransport properties of Bi‑2212 and Bi‑2223 single crystals, the authors demonstrate here that the pseudogap and superconducting fluctuations are distinct phenomena. Their results strongly suggest that the pseudogap arises from preformed Cooper pairing in the BCS–BEC crossover regime, imposing stringent constraints on theoretical descriptions of high‑ T c cuprates beyond the conventional BCS paradigm.

item.title: [7] Highly uniaxial stress-tunable orbital-driven magnetism in CrAs
item.description:
Last authors: Yusuke Nomura, Yoshinori Onose

Authors: Kousuke Ishida, Hsiao-Yi Chen, Shumpei Seto, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Combined experimental and DMFT study of tunable magnetism and orbital correlations in CrAs.

Tags: #material #magnetism #strong-correlations

Abstract: CrAs undergoes a first-order helimagnetic transition accompanied by a huge lattice distortion whose microscopic mechanism remains unresolved. Here, the authors demonstrate through stress-strain measurements that the helimagnetic transition in CrAs is substantially more sensitive to uniaxial stress than to hydrostatic pressure. First-principles calculations reveal that this strong response originates from an entanglement between anisotropic strain and orbital-dependent correlations, showing that local correlations can drive nonlinear elastic responses in strongly correlated systems.
